summary.headline: Trishakti Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 133% YoY to INR 1,551 lakhs, with EBITDA margin of 60.89%.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of INR 1,551 lakhs (up 133% YoY), EBITDA of INR 944 lakhs (up about 141%) and PAT of INR 519 lakhs (up 223%). H1 FY27 revenue was INR 2,989 lakhs, EBITDA INR 1,790 lakhs and PAT INR 949 lakhs. Management said about INR 370 crore of the INR 400 crore FY25-FY27 capex programme (incl. GST) is deployed, and announced "Mission 2030" targeting cumulative gross block above INR 1,000 crore by FY30. Receivable days rose over the past two years; management attributed this to a family settlement and said the cycle will normalise to about 60-65 days by year end.

financial_highlights.metric: Total H1 revenue incl. other income (per Q&A)
Gross block deployed vs FY25-27 programme (per Q&A)
financial_highlights.value: Approx INR 370 crore of INR 400 crore

segments.name: Crane and equipment rental (only segment discussed)
segments.commentary: Fleet includes rough terrain, all terrain, crawler, truck-mounted cranes, AWPs and 70-80m man lifts; management says fleet utilisation has been about 100% for three years. Management claims current ARR is about INR 78 crore after INR 40 crore of machines added in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR 60-65 crore retained; management said it expects to surpass this, with an executable order book of about INR 78 crore and core revenue from operations above INR 75 crore.
Mission 2030: cumulative gross block above INR 1,000 crore by FY30, possibly by FY29 if demand holds; peak revenue of around INR 300 crore cited.
Net debt expected at INR 400-500 crore until FY30; debt-to-equity to stay under 2 for the next 1-1.5 years; deleveraging expected after FY28.
Gross block expected to exceed INR 400 crore by FY27 year end, with INR 90-95 crore (ex-GST) in CWIP to be deployed in Q3 and about INR 125 crore of wind energy capex to arrive from early November.
ARR expected to reach about INR 120 crore from December 2026 to FY28 Q3 as CWIP machines deploy.
UAE and KSA expansion deferred until balance sheet deleverages; paperwork said to be 60-70% complete.
capex_capacity: INR 400 crore FY25-FY27 capex programme: about INR 370 crore deployed (incl. GST), more than 90% complete and ahead of schedule by about six months.
CWIP of about INR 77-78 crore ex-GST (INR 95 crore incl. GST) yet to be deployed in Q3 FY27; contracts reportedly already won for these machines.

Wind energy fleet expansion of about INR 125 crore; machines to arrive from early November; OEMs can supply only 4-5 machines per month in India; management targets replacing 250-300 machines as wind turbines shift from 3.3 to 5.2 MW.

Mission 2030 implies about INR 600-700 crore of incremental capex over three years (about 2.5% of net debt repaid monthly per management); 80-ton tower cranes for data centre work in transit, expected October-November.
Two 70-80m man lifts in fleet; management says about 20-22 such machines exist in India.
demand_pricing: Management says it receives RFQs daily as a central vendor to L&T, Reliance, Tata Steel and others; capex is concentrated in Gujarat and Odisha.
Management says crawler cranes above 150 tonnes are in strong demand; lower-tonnage truck-mounted cranes (80-100 t) are also in demand.
Fleet utilisation about 100% versus an industry figure of about 80% cited in the presentation; management attributes this to 11-12 month contracts versus competitors' 3-4 month contracts.

Management said rental yields are stable and not expected to rise; machine pricing in India is fixed by rental yields. Double-shift operation on 15-20% of machines is said to add about 50% revenue on those machines.
Management said a data centre tower crane generates much higher yield, and specialised 70-80m man lifts earn more than two times current fleet monthly revenue per machine.

qa_highlights.question: Why have debtor days risen over two years, and what is the plan to fix it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed a family settlement from three years ago that extended the cycle; about INR 75 lakh of provision was created this quarter and the cycle should return to about 60-65 days by year end. Management also said about INR 3 crore is over one year old, linked to the family settlement.

qa_highlights.question: How will the capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects net debt of INR 400-500 crore until FY30, funded by bank debt and internal accruals; most FY24-FY25 machines to be free of bank financing by FY28. Only fixed-rate loans apart from the CC limit, which was unused since January; 25 bps rate increase expected on new funding.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on equity dilution and UAE/KSA expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt is the first priority and equity dilution is a final option; it could double the fleet by next year if debt is hard to raise. UAE and KSA expansion depends on internal accruals or equity; KSA local-stake rules reportedly changed after 1 May, allowing 100% ownership.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 revenue guidance INR 60-65 crore or INR 70-80 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance has always been INR 60-65 crore, and that INR 72 crore is only the current ARR; H1 revenue from operations was about INR 30 crore and it expects to beat guidance given the order book and H2 seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: Why are yields not improving with the new fleet, and is sustainability at risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yields are fixed and not expected to rise, but are sustainable; it cited three years of OEM free-of-cost servicing that defers opex, and buying power giving 5-10% machine discount versus competitors.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the receivable cycle elevated, and what caused the move in other current liabilities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said month-end revenue is not billed for 10-12 days because overtime is computed, so trade receivables run high; the move to monthly GST filing shifted about INR 2.5-3 crore of billing, and cash flow should improve from this quarter. Other current liabilities relate to machine funding timing.

risks_watch: Receivable days remain elevated; management promises normalisation to about 60-65 days by Q4 FY27, with the annual report providing clarity.
Mission 2030 assumes fleet utilisation above 90% through FY30; management acknowledged this may be bold.
Debt-to-equity to remain under 2 for 1-1.5 years; net debt of INR 450-500 crore at peak, and possible equity dilution if debt funding is constrained.
Customer concentration in Gujarat and Odisha capex cycle; no soft commitments from customers for expansion, per management.
Machine import dependence above 250 tonnes and rising global machine costs; yields not expected to rise.
Gross block and revenue timing depend on delivery of wind energy and tower crane machines, now in transit.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on demand, utilisation and Mission 2030, but cautious on near-term balance sheet: management repeatedly deferred UAE/KSA expansion and equity dilution decisions. Answers on receivables and FY27 revenue guidance were somewhat repetitive, and some answers on yields and imported machine pricing were unclear.
key_quotes: Mission 2030 is not simply about owning more machines. It is about building a stronger Trishakti with greater capabilities, deeper customer relationships, and a larger role in India's infrastructure growth story.
We have already won contracts for all these INR 95 crores worth of machines.
Our guiding principle is simple. We want to grow with India, build for the long-term, and turn our ambition into measurable execution.
